scheme_name: Futkar Sabji, Phal-Phool Vikreta Hetu Taraju, Baat Evan Tokari Sahaayata Yojana
description:
The Futkar Sabji, Phal-Phool Vikreta Hetu Taraju, Baat Evan Tokari Sahaayata Yojana is a welfare scheme initiated by the Government of India to support vendors engaged in the sale of vegetables, fruits, and flowers. 

This scheme was launched on 1st April 2021. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance to street vendors who sell fresh produce. 

The government aims to enhance the income of these vendors by providing them with necessary tools and equipment. 

The specific goal is to improve the livelihood of at least 1 million vendors across the country within the first year of implementation. 

The scheme targets vendors who are registered under the PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) scheme. 

Eligible beneficiaries can receive financial assistance of up to ₹10,000. 

This amount is intended for the purchase of weighing scales, baskets, and other necessary equipment. 

The scheme also aims to promote hygienic practices among vendors to ensure the quality of food sold to consumers. 

The eligibility criteria for the scheme include being a registered street vendor under the PM SVANidhi scheme. 

Applicants must be engaged in the sale of vegetables, fruits, or flowers. 

There are no specific age limits for applicants. 

However, the income criteria state that the annual income of the vendor should not exceed ₹1 lakh. 

The application process is straightforward and can be completed online. 

Vendors must visit the official website of the PM SVANidhi scheme. 

They need to fill out the application form available on the website. 

Required documents include proof of identity, proof of address, and registration under the PM SVANidhi scheme. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be verified by the concerned authorities. 

The timeline for the disbursement of funds is typically within 30 days of application approval. 

The funds are transferred directly to the bank account of the beneficiary. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. 

The contact details for the ministry can be found on their official website. 

The scheme is part of a larger initiative to promote self-employment among urban poor. 

The government has allocated ₹500 crores for the implementation of this scheme in the financial year 2021-2022. 

This funding is aimed at supporting the initial rollout and ensuring that vendors have access to the necessary resources. 

The scheme also focuses on providing training to vendors on best practices in hygiene and customer service. 

Training sessions are organized by local municipal bodies in collaboration with NGOs. 

The government has set a target to conduct training for at least 500,000 vendors in the first year. 

The scheme is expected to benefit not only the vendors but also consumers by ensuring better quality and hygiene in food products. 

The initiative is part of the government's broader strategy to uplift the informal sector. 

Street vendors play a crucial role in urban economies by providing affordable food options. 

The scheme aims to formalize their operations and integrate them into the mainstream economy. 

Additionally, the government is working on creating a digital platform for vendors to promote their products. 

This platform will help vendors reach a larger customer base and increase their sales. 

The scheme also encourages the use of eco-friendly packaging materials. 

Vendors are provided with information on sustainable practices to reduce environmental impact. 

The government is monitoring the implementation of the scheme through regular assessments. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme further. 

The success of the scheme will be evaluated based on the increase in income of the vendors. 

The government aims for at least a 30% increase in the income of beneficiaries within the first year. 

The scheme is expected to create a positive ripple effect in local economies. 

By supporting vendors, the government is also promoting local agriculture. 

The initiative encourages vendors to source their products from local farmers. 

This not only supports farmers but also ensures fresh produce for consumers. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from various stakeholders in the urban economy. 

Local bodies are actively involved in promoting the scheme among vendors. 

Awareness campaigns are conducted to ensure that eligible vendors are informed about the benefits. 

The government is also collaborating with financial institutions to provide additional support to vendors. 

This includes access to micro-loans for expanding their businesses. 

The Futkar Sabji, Phal-Phool Vikreta Hetu Taraju, Baat Evan Tokari Sahaayata Yojana is a significant step towards empowering street vendors. 

It reflects the government's commitment to improving the livelihoods of the urban poor. 

The scheme is expected to have a lasting impact on the socio-economic conditions of street vendors. 

By providing financial assistance and training, the government is fostering entrepreneurship among vendors. 

This initiative is a crucial part of the larger vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat. 

It aims to make India self-reliant by supporting small businesses and informal sectors. 

The government continues to monitor the progress of the scheme to ensure its effectiveness. 

Regular updates and reports are published to keep stakeholders informed. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's efforts in promoting inclusive growth. 

It highlights the importance of supporting the informal sector in urban areas. 

The Futkar Sabji, Phal-Phool Vikreta Hetu Taraju, Baat Evan Tokari Sahaayata Yojana is a vital initiative for the upliftment of street vendors in India.
